section_subtext.failed: Companies whose primary OA program has been discontinued, or whose pivotal trial(s) failed with no confirmed path forward.
section_subtext.pending: Programs still in active development — dosing, recruiting, or awaiting a regulatory decision. No verdict yet, or a verdict still being contested.
section_subtext.momentum: Programs with genuinely positive recent data and forward motion.
section_subtext.none: Shortlisted for historical OA-related trial activity, but with no drug currently in development.

companies.name: AstraZeneca
companies.mechanism: NGF/TNF-α bispecific fusion protein
companies.finding: AZ's most advanced OA asset was discontinued around Q1 2025 — not a trial failure, but part of a full pain/neuroscience R&D exit. Two earlier candidates (MEDI-578, AZD1386) were dropped in the early 2010s. No musculoskeletal category remains on AZ's pipeline page.

companies.name: Boehringer Ingelheim
companies.mechanism: Bradykinin B1-receptor antagonist
companies.finding: Its only OA trial (Phase 1, 2014) produced no efficacy readout, and later attempts in two other indications also failed (2020, 2023). No trial of any kind registered since — effectively shelved.

companies.name: Centrexion
companies.mechanism: Trans-capsaicin intra-articular injection
companies.finding: Both pivotal Phase 3 trials (VICTORY-1/2) missed their individual primary endpoint around 2021. A pooled post-hoc analysis was positive at ACR 2023, but no confirmed regulatory path or update has surfaced since.

companies.name: Grünenthal
companies.mechanism: Resiniferatoxin (TRPV1 agonist)
companies.finding: A 3-trial global Phase 3 program completed by mid-2025. Posted results show only a marginal pain gap over placebo, and the asset has since quietly disappeared from Grünenthal's own pipeline page despite 2023 guidance of a 2025 filing. Inferred discontinued — no company confirmation found.

companies.name: GSK
companies.mechanism: Anti-CCL17 antibody
companies.finding: Phase 2 trial “MARS-17” was terminated for futility in late 2024. A second candidate, otilimab (anti-GM-CSF), had only marginal hand-OA data and died with its broader rheumatoid arthritis program in Oct 2022. No active OA pipeline remains.

companies.name: Johnson & Johnson
companies.mechanism: Anti-NGF antibody
companies.finding: Phase 3 OA program discontinued March 2016 for portfolio prioritization; rights returned to originator Amgen. No revival found, and no other confirmed J&J OA pipeline asset exists today.

companies.name: Kolon TissueGene
companies.mechanism: Allogeneic cell + TGF-β1 gene therapy
companies.finding: Korean approval was revoked in 2019 after a cell-identity mislabeling scandal. The first of two US pivotal trials, ACTiVION-II, missed both co-primary endpoints in July 2026, triggering a sharp stock drop. The second trial's October 2026 readout is described by the company as decisive.

companies.name: Merck (MSD)
companies.mechanism: COX-2 inhibitor / cathepsin K inhibitor
companies.finding: No active OA program today. Rofecoxib (Vioxx) was withdrawn in 2004 over cardiovascular risk; odanacatib was discontinued in 2016 over stroke risk.

companies.name: Novartis
companies.mechanism: Cartilage-regeneration DMOAD
companies.finding: Early Phase 1/2a data looked encouraging, but the pivotal Phase 2b trial (ONWARDS) was terminated in 2024 after showing no dose-response on cartilage thickness — every dose arm lost cartilage at essentially the placebo rate. Discontinued; absent from the FY2025 20-F entirely.

companies.name: Pfizer
companies.mechanism: Anti-NGF antibody
companies.finding: Phase 3 efficacy was real, but joint-safety signals (rapidly progressive OA) drove a 19–1 FDA Advisory Committee vote against approval. Pfizer and Lilly discontinued the global program in October 2021. Tanezumab hasn't appeared in Pfizer's 10-K pipeline text in any year since.

companies.name: Regeneron
companies.mechanism: Anti-NGF antibody (w/ Teva)
companies.finding: Phase 3 program hit the same joint-safety wall as tanezumab and was discontinued in Nov 2022. Regeneron and Teva have continued publishing the already-completed trial data through 2026 — legacy reporting, not renewed development.

companies.name: Unity Biotechnology
companies.mechanism: Senolytic (p53/MDM2 inhibitor)
companies.finding: Failed its Phase 2 primary endpoint in Aug 2020. The company pivoted to ophthalmology senolytics, then began winding down in 2025: Nasdaq delisting, shareholder-approved liquidation, and formal SEC deregistration in Jan 2026.

companies.name: Biosplice
companies.mechanism: Wnt-pathway inhibitor (intra-articular)
companies.finding: All three pivotal Phase 3 trials missed their primary endpoint in the full patient population (2022, 2024). Biosplice filed an NDA anyway in January 2026, leaning on a long-term extension trial and post-hoc subgroup data — with no Fast Track or Breakthrough designation found. The most consequential open question on this board.

companies.name: Eupraxia
companies.mechanism: Extended-release intra-articular steroid
companies.finding: Positive Phase 2b data (published in Lancet Rheumatology) and FDA Fast Track once made this a strong prospect. A Phase 3 was announced in Feb 2024, but no evidence of actual dosing was found, and the company now says it's “evaluating funding alternatives” — effectively on hold, seeking a partner.

companies.name: Genascence
companies.mechanism: IL-1Ra gene therapy
companies.finding: Phase 1b met its 12-month safety endpoint in May 2025, and the FDA has granted both Fast Track and RMAT designation. A Phase 2b/3 design is reportedly agreed with FDA for a 2026 start — but no confirmation of actual dosing was found as of this pull.

companies.name: Novo Nordisk
companies.mechanism: GLP-1/amylin dual agonist
companies.finding: Phase 3 trials AMAZE 5 and AMAZE 6 are recruiting, with a 2028 completion estimate. The program was first named in an SEC filing only in Q1 2026 — a genuinely early-stage bet, not yet a story with a verdict.

companies.name: Pacira
companies.mechanism: Steroid injection (marketed) + gene therapy (pipeline)
companies.finding: Zilretta had its first-ever revenue decline in FY2025 (-1%), though 2026 quarters show reacceleration. PCRX-201's Phase 2 enrollment was announced “concluded” twice, seven months apart, without reconciliation — flagged, not yet explained.

companies.name: Eli Lilly
companies.mechanism: GLP-1/GIP/amylin-class (via weight loss)
companies.finding: Retatrutide's OA data was the field's best recent news: positive Phase 3 topline in Dec 2025 (WOMAC pain improved ~75% vs. ~40% placebo), with a single BLA covering obesity + sleep apnea + knee OA planned for Q1 2027. That filing now carries added regulatory risk: Lilly and the FDA are still litigating whether retatrutide legally qualifies as a biologic at all (12-yr vs. 5-yr exclusivity), with oral arguments set for Sept 24, 2026 — about six months before the targeted filing. Orforglipron and eloralintide's own OA readouts aren't due until 2028; a fourth asset, LY4065967, has almost no public paper trail.

companies.name: Levicept
companies.mechanism: Anti-NGF/p75 receptor fusion protein
companies.finding: A differentiated take on the anti-NGF mechanism that sank tanezumab and fasinumab. Full Phase 2 results (518 patients) published in The Lancet, March 2026: met its primary endpoint at every dose, with no increased joint-safety signal. FDA accepted the IND in Jan 2026.

companies.name: Organon
companies.mechanism: No active candidate
companies.finding: Organon's own pipeline page lists Women's Health and General Medicine as its sole therapeutic priorities; osteoarthritis isn't mentioned. All OA-linked trial history traces to legacy Merck etoricoxib data, a drug never approved in the US.

companies.name: 4B Technologies Limited
companies.mechanism: TrkA activator; non-opioid pain signaling modulator
companies.finding: Phase 1 study of FB1003 in healthy and OA-pain subjects is recruiting with completion estimated Feb 2026; no efficacy data or partnership news found beyond the trial listing.

companies.name: Anterogen Co., Ltd.
companies.mechanism: Adult stem cell replacement therapy for joint/cartilage degeneration
companies.finding: Open-label Phase 1 dose-escalation trial in Grade III/IV knee OA is active but not recruiting, completion estimated May 2026; no results disclosed yet beyond the registration.

companies.name: CELL Technologies Inc.
companies.mechanism: Point-of-care autologous cell therapy delivering bone-marrow progenitor cells via intra-articular injection
companies.finding: The Pan-Canadian ACCELERATE3 trial is a Phase 3, 374-patient randomized study comparing BMAC to standard of care with 48-week follow-up; no results reported yet.

companies.name: Enlivex Therapeutics Ltd.
companies.mechanism: Immunomodulatory macrophage reprogramming therapy
companies.finding: Phase I/II data in knee OA showed durable pain reduction and function improvement at 6 months versus placebo, including reported avoidance of knee replacement in some patients; presented at OARSI 2025 and EULAR 2025.

companies.name: ICM Co. Ltd.
companies.mechanism: Intra-articular AAV gene therapy expressing Nkx3.2 to support cartilage/synovium
companies.finding: Interim Phase 1/2a data showed pain reduction in 6 of 8 and cartilage thickness preserved/improved in 5 of 8 low-dose subjects through Week 52, a promising early first-in-human signal presented at OARSI.

companies.name: Laboratorios Silanes S.A. de C.V.
companies.mechanism: Fixed-dose COX-2 NSAID plus acetaminophen for multi-mechanism OA pain relief
companies.finding: Phase 3 "PRECEDENT" trial comparing the combination to celecoxib alone in acute OA exacerbation completed enrollment with results estimated ~Oct 2025; a related long-acting injectable formulation was also tested. No results published yet.

companies.name: Nova Vita Laboratory
companies.mechanism: Acellular filtered human amniotic fluid delivering growth factors/cytokines intra-articularly
companies.finding: Small 24-subject Phase 1/2 randomized, placebo-controlled trial in knee OA is underway measuring WOMAC and biomarkers; no results or funding news found beyond the registration and company site.

companies.name: PharmaResearch Co.,Ltd
companies.mechanism: Intra-articular hyaluronic acid viscosupplementation
companies.finding: Hyruan is an already-marketed, established HA product line (not an active pipeline candidate); Hyruan ONE's single-shot regimen has shown efficacy comparable to Hyruan Plus's three-shot regimen. No new trial activity found.

companies.name: Sclnow Biotechnology Co., Ltd.
companies.mechanism: Allogeneic umbilical-cord-derived mesenchymal stem cell injection for cartilage defect/OA
companies.finding: Trial NCT03383081 evaluating efficacy/safety across cartilage defect severities is listed as recruiting as of December 2025; third-party trackers place the asset at Phase 2. No results found.

companies.name: TricelX Inc.
companies.mechanism: Allogeneic umbilical-cord-derived mesenchymal stem cell injection for knee OA
companies.finding: TricelX filed an IND and requested RMAT designation for XytriX in March 2026, and the FDA has since issued a Study May Proceed letter clearing the Phase 1/2 trial to begin — a genuine near-term regulatory milestone, though no efficacy data exists yet.

companies.name: 4Moving Biotech
companies.mechanism: Intra-articular GLP-1 receptor agonist (DMOAD candidate)
companies.finding: Phase I safety met endpoint; company just landed FDA Fast Track designation and IND clearance in April 2026 for knee OA with synovitis, a strong signal for its size.

companies.name: ArthroBiologix Inc.
companies.mechanism: Viscosupplement paired with a short-acting corticosteroid, intra-articular
companies.finding: Small orthobiologics research outfit running a hip OA/impingement trial combining the injection with physical therapy; no results or company disclosures found beyond the trial listings.

companies.name: CarthroniX, Inc.
companies.mechanism: Small-molecule gp130/IL-6 pathway modulator, intra-articular
companies.finding: Preclinical data in rats and dogs (published in Science Translational Medicine) supported a 2022 $2.25M financing round; Phase 1/2a human trial not slated to start until 2026.

companies.name: Fujian Shengdi Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.
companies.mechanism: Dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist; OA benefit likely indirect via weight loss
companies.finding: Hengrui/Kailera's ribupatide has strong momentum in obesity (positive Phase 2, now Phase 3 KaiNETIC), but no public disclosure ties it specifically to the OA trial beyond the registration itself.
companies.date_label: Phase 3, ongoing (parent program has momentum in obesity)

companies.name: Immunis, Inc.
companies.mechanism: Stem-cell-derived secretome targeting OA-associated muscle atrophy (sarcopenia), not the joint
companies.finding: Completed Phase 1/2a showed improved walk distance, gait speed, and no severe adverse events; advancing to a larger Phase 2b (STEM-MYO) trial.

companies.name: Magellan Stem Cells
companies.mechanism: Off-the-shelf allogeneic adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells, intra-articular
companies.finding: Phase I/IIa (40 patients) showed safety and efficacy signals; company is moving to a 573-patient Phase III trial planned for late 2025, a big step for a company this size.

companies.name: Nuwacell Biotechnologies Co., Ltd.
companies.mechanism: iPSC-derived mesenchymal stromal cells, intra-articular
companies.finding: Reportedly the first iPSC-derived MSC product cleared for clinical trials in China; multiple active trials including a novel zirconium-89 biodistribution study, but no efficacy results disclosed yet.

companies.name: R3 Medical Research
companies.mechanism: Regenerative allograft (growth factors, cytokines, HA, extracellular vesicles), intra-articular knee injection
companies.finding: Early feasibility study only; no results or disclosures found beyond the trial registration.

companies.name: Shandong Suncadia Medicine Co., Ltd.
companies.mechanism: Undisclosed mechanism; oral analgesic being tested across knee OA pain and gout flare pain
companies.finding: Phase Ib dose-finding trial (~200 patients) recruiting; no public disclosure of mechanism or results found beyond the trial registrations.

companies.name: UnicoCell Biomed CO. LTD
companies.mechanism: Allogeneic adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells, intra-articular
companies.finding: Phase III trial completed patient enrollment in November 2025 with both TFDA and FDA approvals in hand; earlier data showed faster pain/function improvement than hyaluronic acid.

companies.name: Addpharma Inc.
companies.mechanism: Mechanism undisclosed; dose-ranging analgesic/anti-inflammatory candidate
companies.finding: Phase 2 dose-finding trial in knee OA with low/medium/high arms vs. an active comparator; no results or mechanism detail disclosed beyond the trial registration.

companies.name: Avidence Therapeutics
companies.mechanism: Disease-modifying candidate from a "cartilage regeneration platform," specific target undisclosed
companies.finding: Small NY biotech (founded 2018) with a broader regenerative-pathway platform; AVD275 is Phase 1, no results or partnerships found beyond investor-database listings.

companies.name: CellSeed Inc.
companies.mechanism: Allogeneic cartilage cell-sheet transplantation combined with osteotomy and marrow stimulation
companies.finding: Japanese cell-sheet engineering program with over a decade of supportive academic research; now in Phase III seeking PMD Act approval, a more mature evidence base than most peers on this list.

companies.name: Glaceum
companies.mechanism: Oral small-molecule inflammation-mediator inhibitor
companies.finding: Korean biotech also developing this asset for obesity/NASH; OA program is Phase 2a (26-week trial), no results reported yet.

companies.name: Jiangsu Aosaikang Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.
companies.mechanism: Topical analgesic, specific target undisclosed
companies.finding: Established Chinese pharma running a Phase 1/2 dose-finding trial; NMPA accepted the clinical trial application in 2023, no efficacy data yet.

companies.name: Mather's Pharm. Co., Ltd.
companies.mechanism: Oral multi-plant botanical extract, anti-inflammatory/chondroprotective
companies.finding: Phase 4 (post-marketing) study implies the product is already approved/sold; a related botanical (PG201/Layla) showed significant pain/function benefit in an earlier published trial, though link to Laybon isn't fully confirmed.

companies.name: OrthoTrophix, Inc
companies.mechanism: Intra-articular MEPE-peptide injection intended to activate cartilage-forming cells
companies.finding: Genuine published disease-modification data: Phase 2a showed significant knee function gains and reduced bone-shape/cartilage deterioration vs. placebo; Phase 2b trial (mild-severe knee OA) completed enrollment early in 2026, readout pending.

companies.name: RegenLab France SAS
companies.mechanism: Intra-articular PRP + cross-linked hyaluronic acid combination device
companies.finding: Established PRP device maker (since 2003) running a three-arm trial vs. Hylan G-F 20 and placebo; this is a label-expansion/device study for an already-marketed product family, not an early pipeline bet. No results yet.

companies.name: Shanghai AbelZeta Ltd.
companies.mechanism: Allogeneic mesenchymal progenitor cells injected intra-articularly to reduce inflammation and support cartilage repair
companies.finding: Program originated at AbelZeta but was spun off into ElpasBio in 2023; ElpasBio completed Phase III enrollment (500+ patients) in May 2026 and signed a China commercialization deal with Fosun Kairos, aiming to be the first disease-modifying regenerative product for knee OA.

companies.name: VivaTech International, Inc.
companies.mechanism: Ultrasound-cavitation-extracted stromal vascular fraction cells (no enzymes) combined with autologous PRP
companies.finding: Small regenerative-medicine company running an open-label Phase 2 trial (targeting eventual expansion to ~4,000 patients); no trial results yet, though a related published case series on similar SVF+PRP therapy showed strong pain relief.

companies.name: Ageless Biotech, Inc.
companies.mechanism: Adipose-derived stem cell (SVF) intra-articular injection
companies.finding: FDA-accepted IND; Phase IIb trial recruiting since May 2025, completion est. March 2028. No efficacy or funding news beyond the IND announcement.

companies.name: Belief BioMed (Beijing) Co., Ltd
companies.mechanism: AAV gene therapy delivering anti-inflammatory protein intra-articularly
companies.finding: NMPA IND cleared in China; Phase 1/2 trial began October 2025, completion est. Dec 2027. Early investigator-initiated data described as promising but not detailed publicly.

companies.name: Doron Therapeutics Inc.
companies.mechanism: Placental-tissue-derived regenerative biologic, intra-articular knee injection
companies.finding: FDA Fast Track and RMAT designations; first patients dosed in Phase 3 (~300 patients) as of Oct 2025 after a positive End-of-Phase 2 meeting; raised $11M to fund the advance.

companies.name: Hangzhou Sciwind Biosciences Co., Ltd.
companies.mechanism: Long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist, weight-loss mediated joint-load reduction
companies.finding: Commercially approved in China for obesity/T2D; no OA-specific trial data or disclosure found, but mechanism parallels Lilly's tirzepatide and Novo Nordisk's semaglutide knee-OA programs already tracked.

companies.name: KeyBioscience AG
companies.mechanism: Dual amylin/calcitonin receptor agonist (DACRA), weight loss + analgesic + cartilage-protective
companies.finding: Preclinical data (2024) showed pain and weight reduction in a metabolic OA rat model; Phase 2 trial actively recruiting in obese OA patients. No clinical results yet.

companies.name: Medipost Co Ltd.
companies.mechanism: Umbilical-cord-blood allogeneic MSC therapy for cartilage repair
companies.finding: CARTISTEM already marketed in Korea since 2012; met all endpoints in Japan Phase 3 and FDA-cleared US Phase 3 dosed its first patient July 2026. High Hyal Plus and SMUP-IA-01 have no public disclosure beyond trial registration.

companies.name: Paradigm Biopharmaceuticals Ltd.
companies.mechanism: Disease-modifying candidate, anti-inflammatory/cartilage-protective glycosaminoglycan
companies.finding: ASX-listed; Phase IIb trial met secondary endpoints with reduced bone marrow lesions and a disease-modification signal; new 2026 research partnership with City St George's, University of London.

companies.name: Saol Therapeutics Inc
companies.mechanism: Chemoneurolytic intra-articular injection (CYCLOPHLEX platform) for OA pain
companies.finding: Completed Phase II COMPASS enrollment; positive End-of-Phase II FDA meeting (April 2025) cleared a path to pivotal trial, but no efficacy data published yet.

companies.name: TBF Genie Tissulaire
companies.mechanism: Devitalized umbilical cord amniotic membrane implant for joint interposition (hand OA)
companies.finding: Small French tissue bank (est. 1992); active recruiting trial for PIP joint OA, no results or funding news found — appears to be a niche academic study rather than a commercial push.

companies.name: ZetrOZ, Inc.
companies.mechanism: Wearable therapeutic ultrasound device combined with topical NSAID patch
companies.finding: Device already FDA-cleared and commercially marketed; combination trial with diclofenac patch ongoing (NCT04391842), no published results for the combination yet.

companies.name: Akan Biosciences, LLC
companies.mechanism: Autologous adipose-derived stem cell therapy for knee OA
companies.finding: Phase 1/2 trial registered (not yet recruiting per CT.gov) though company site claims it's already in Phase 2; broad early-stage regenerative platform with plans to expand into other indications. No funding/partnership data found.

companies.name: Bioventus LLC
companies.mechanism: Allogeneic placental tissue particulate, intra-articular injection for knee OA
companies.finding: Public orthobiologics leader (NASDAQ: BVS) known for marketed HA injectables; PTP-001 has advanced from Phase 1 through Phase 2 to a recruiting Phase 3 trial, though the Phase 3 is oddly sponsored by a related entity, "Doron Therapeutics," not Bioventus directly. No efficacy data yet.

companies.name: DuoGenic StemCells Corporation (DGSC)
companies.mechanism: Autologous peripheral blood mononuclear cell injection for knee OA
companies.finding: Phase 2/3 trial registered but not yet recruiting; no company website, press coverage, or additional disclosure found anywhere beyond the CT.gov listing.

companies.name: Healeon Medical Inc
companies.mechanism: Autologous adipose stem/stromal cells plus HD-PRP, injected for OA
companies.finding: Small orthobiologics device maker running a recruiting NA-phase registry-style study; corporate site now redirects to Bimini Health Tech, whose PRP product pages emphasize bone-graft use rather than OA specifically.

companies.name: LG Chem
companies.mechanism: Cross-linked hyaluronic acid viscosupplement injection for knee OA
companies.finding: Confirmed as a real, already-marketed HA product in Korea (not an early pipeline asset) — multiple competitors run non-inferiority trials against it as the market reference standard. No new R&D news found.

companies.name: Nature Cell Co. Ltd.
companies.mechanism: Autologous adipose-derived stem cell therapy for knee OA
companies.finding: Deepest trial history in this batch, spanning Phase 1/2 (2008) through a completed Phase 3 (2020) to an active Phase 2b/3a study running through 2027; company references a January 2025 FDA IND approval for US development, but Korean marketing-approval status remains unresolved despite years of trials.

companies.name: Peptinov SAS
companies.mechanism: Anti-IL-6 active immunotherapy ("vaccine") inducing patient antibodies against interleukin-6
companies.finding: Completed Phase 1 dose-escalation safety study; has since registered a Phase 2 trial in inflammatory-phenotype knee OA (not yet recruiting), using a distinctive vaccine-style mechanism. Company website unreachable; no other disclosure found.

companies.name: Scarcell Therapeutics S.A.S.
companies.mechanism: Allogeneic gingival fibroblast cell therapy, single knee injection, immune-tolerant (no immunosuppression needed)
companies.finding: First-in-human Phase 1 trial recruiting; backed by an unusually strong preclinical package — 800+ companion animals (dogs, racehorses) with up to 2-year follow-up and US patents on the cell product and process. No human data yet.

companies.name: TRB Chemedica
companies.mechanism: IL-1 inhibitor positioned as a potential disease/structure-modifying OA therapy
companies.finding: Established Swiss company selling diacerein internationally (not FDA-approved in the US); running an ongoing Phase 3 structure-modification trial using MRI cartilage-volume endpoints, following an earlier completed Phase 3 vs. celecoxib. No new efficacy results found.
